title: Sprint-and-Free-Throw
description: Players run a sprint, then shoot two free throws while their heart rate is high, as they would after a hard possession.

content.objective: Keep the free-throw routine and make shots when tired.
content.setup: Two or three players per basket; one at the line, others on the baseline.
content.organization: Rotate after each player's two shots.
instructions: Sprint baseline to baseline and back (one down-and-back).
Go straight to the free-throw line.
Take one deep breath as part of the routine, then shoot two.
Next player sprints while the previous one rebounds.
coachingPoints: Use the breath to slow down the heart.
Legs give the power when the arms are tired.
commonMistakes: Rushing up to the line and shooting immediately.
Short shots because the legs are not used.
content.safety: Build the number of sprints gradually; players who feel dizzy stop and rest.
progressions: Must make both or repeat the sprint.
variations: Defensive slides instead of a sprint.
Shoot from the elbow after the sprint.
successCriteria: At least 70% of free throws made over the session.
content.gameApplication: Free throws often come after the hardest possessions of the game, when players are tired.
